review.summary: Scoped rough-whole-route checks are supported by the supplied native frames and trace (the Chicago image is only the target reference, not the build). Connected 52 s replay: walking (player displacement 26.2 m) and driving (vehicle displacement 20.1 m) both occur. Combat is real in both directions: two Mouse0 shots at t=7.53/9.22 register first_aim_collider "Rival" and drop rival HP 3→2→1 with viewport_contains_center true, while enemy attacks separately reduce player health (visible 100→92→80, and 56 at failure). Pursuit arms before the clear window (level 0→3→2→3 early, wanted stars visible in frames) and the escape is genuine: far_pursuit_levels [0], longest continuous escape 2.9 s vs required 2.0 s, rival motion 4.47 m during driving, pursuit back to 0 at ~18 m distance. Failure is real, not scripted mid-run: frame-008 (t=31) shows the MISSION FAILED / "Ran out of time" banner at t=30.08 with health 56; frame-009 (t=32.5, post-reset, restarts=1) shows HEALTH 100, "WANTED ...", and the reset 30 s grab-the-YELLOW-parcel objective with the yellow cube present. Retry ends in frame-012 (t=47.2) with ★ DELIVERY COMPLETE ★ at the green pad, matching the trace's delivery edge (distance 1.21 m, mission "complete", negligible 0.0026 m penetration). HUD is readable and state-consistent in every frame (health, wanted stars, objective/help lines, mission banners); audio_peak_rms 0.206 establishes a live mixer signal per the stated standard, though sound quality remains unproven. Build/compile clean, all ten regressions pass, duration 52 s is within the 240 s budget. Minor rough-stage polish observed but not route-breaking: the yellow parcel cube still appears near the fence in frame-010 after the "parcel in hand" state (pickup t=39.43), the world remains placeholder-grade (flat brown plane, bare skyline), and the delivery pad beam overlaps the car body — acceptable dev art for this stage. This is a scoped PASS, not final game acceptance.
